source_caption:
One of the greatest films ever put on a screen! 

Cinema Paradiso is partly based on director Giuseppe Tornatore’s own childhood in Sicily, where he first fell in love with movies.

It’s a nostalgic love letter to cinema, telling the story of Salvatore, a successful filmmaker who returns to his small Sicilian hometown after many years. There, he recalls his childhood during the late 1940s and 1950s, when he discovered his passion for film at the local movie theater, Cinema Paradiso.

As a boy nicknamed Toto, Salvatore formed a deep friendship with Alfredo, the projectionist, who became his mentor and father figure. Alfredo taught him about movies, life, and the importance of following his dreams - even if that meant leaving the town.

The film’s famous ending - a reel of censored kissing scenes — was inspired by real Italian censorship laws that once banned intimate moments from films. Originally 173 minutes long, the movie was cut down to 124 minutes for its international release, a version that went on to win the Oscar for Best Foreign Language Film and the Grand Prix at Cannes. Its heartfelt celebration of the magic of cinema even inspired the restoration of old Italian theaters that were in danger of closing.

source_details.synopsis: Cinema Paradiso (Italian: Nuovo Cinema Paradiso, Italian pronunciation: [ˈnwɔːvo ˈtʃiːnema paraˈdiːzo], lit. 'New Paradise Cinema') is a 1988 coming-of-age comedy-drama film written and directed by Giuseppe Tornatore. Set in a fictional small Sicilian town, called Giancaldo, the film centres on the friendship between a young boy and an aging projectionist who works at the titular movie theatre. The Italian-French co-production stars Philippe Noiret, Jacques Perrin, Antonella Attili, Pupella Maggio and Salvatore Cascio.
